title: A magazine cover
text: The magazine cover [show|shows|'The cover' is singular, so add -s.] a young woman in the foreground. She is wearing [a expensive|an expensive|Use 'an' before a vowel sound.] dress, which suggests that she is wealthy. The bright [colour|colours|There are several colours here, so use the plural.] create a happy mood. The target audience is probably young [woman|women|More than one person, so use the plural 'women'.].

title: A sports advert
text: The advert represents the man as [strongly|strong|After 'represent someone as', use an adjective.] and successful. The camera angle makes him [looks|look|After 'make someone', use the base verb.] powerful. This [reinforce|reinforces|'This' is singular, so add -s.] the stereotype that men should be strong. There [is|are|'There are' + a plural noun.] no women in the image, so it is not a realistic representation.

title: A news photograph
text: The photo was [take|taken|Passive: was + past participle 'taken'.] in a hospital. The nurse's facial expression is [care|caring|You need an adjective here: caring.]. In the background, there are many [patient|patients|After 'many', use a plural noun.]. The headline describes her as a hero, which creates [an positive|a positive|Use 'a' before a consonant sound.] representation of nurses.

title: A charity poster
text: The purpose [for|of|We say 'the purpose of' something.] the poster is to make people recycle. It uses a close-up of a turtle, which looks [vulnerability|vulnerable|After 'looks', you need an adjective.]. The dark lighting [create|creates|'The lighting' is singular, so add -s.] a serious mood. The poster has a strong effect [to|on|We say 'an effect on' someone.] the audience.

title: Two family adverts
text: The first advert represents the family as [tradition|traditional|You need an adjective: traditional.]. The mother [is cook|is cooking|Present continuous: is + -ing.] in the kitchen, and the father [read|reads|'The father' is singular, so add -s.] a newspaper. This is a stereotypical image. The second advert [challenge|challenges|'The second advert' is singular, so add -s.] this idea because the father is cooking.

title: A perfume advert
text: The setting is [an luxury|a luxury|Use 'a' before a consonant sound.] hotel. The model is young and [attraction|attractive|You need an adjective here: attractive.]. She [looking|is looking|Present continuous needs 'is' + -ing.] away from the camera, which makes her seem mysterious. The slogan [are|is|'The slogan' is singular, so use 'is'.] written in gold letters.

title: A football magazine
text: The headline describes the team as [success|successful|After 'describe someone as', use an adjective.]. The players [is|are|'The players' is plural, so use 'are'.] celebrating in the foreground. The bright lighting [create|creates|'The lighting' is singular, so add -s.] a happy mood. However, there are no women [on|in|We say 'in the image'.] the image.

title: A charity advert
text: The advert shows [a old|an old|Use 'an' before a vowel sound.] man sitting alone. His facial expression [suggest|suggests|'His facial expression' is singular, so add -s.] that he is lonely. The audience may [feels|feel|After 'may', use the base verb.] sympathy for him. The purpose of the advert is to make people [donating|donate|After 'make someone', use the base verb.] money.
